title: File management tools either have duplicate context menu items or none at all in extended menu

fix_assessment.rationale: The report provides a concrete modern/classic menu comparison and screenshots, but the producing provider for each duplicate or missing command is not yet isolated. Current source confirms that the tools have package-backed modern verbs and classic shell registrations; that is a testable hypothesis, not proof of a shared defect.

proposed_fixes.title: Align context-menu visibility with each tool's registration mode
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Windows 11 can expose both package-backed modern verbs and classic shell handlers, and the providers may not consistently agree with each tool's selected menu mode. Image Resizer also has both a package manifest and runtime-registered classic handler. The current report does not identify which provider causes each duplicate or missing entry.
plan: Reproduce the reported modes separately for File Locksmith and PowerRename and test Image Resizer independently, counting each command in the Windows 11 default menu and Show more options menu.

In a disposable Store-install test account, correlate each visible entry with its package-backed IExplorerCommand or classic shell handler; compare registrations before and after a supported update without deleting user registry entries.
Change only the provider and visibility guard demonstrated to be wrong, then add a tool-specific UI test that asserts exactly one command on each supported surface for each menu mode.
Keep Image Resizer separate because it does not expose the same extended-only setting; coordinate partial coverage with #20255 and #49416 without treating them as a complete fix.
verification: On current stable, verify exactly one command for each enabled utility in the default and extended menus, and verify the configured extended-only behavior for File Locksmith and PowerRename.
Test Image Resizer with an image file and test File Locksmith/PowerRename with both image-file and folder selections where supported.
Repeat after a supported Store update or repair in a disposable account and confirm the duplicate does not return; do not use registry deletion as a workaround.

confidence.rationale: The screenshots and menu-mode comparison establish a repeatable symptom. Source confirms modern package and classic registration paths, but no executed provider-by-provider matrix identifies the failing registration or proves that all three tools share one root cause.

issue_context.summary: File Locksmith, PowerRename, and Image Resizer are duplicated in the extended context menu in one configuration, while the configured commands disappear in extended-only mode.
known_information: The reporter uses PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store and supplied screenshots for combined and extended-only menu configurations.
The reporter says File Locksmith and PowerRename are set to appear in both default and extended menus; Image Resizer appears for image files.
A later commenter reports that registry-removal workarounds only last until a PowerToys update.
The reporter says existing historical issue #30321 covers only Image Resizer and asks that this three-tool report not be treated as fully covered by that partial duplicate.
The November 4 comment proposes a Windows menu-composition theory, but it does not include a provider-level test or registration trace.
inferences: The package-backed modern verbs and classic shell handlers could interact differently across the default and extended menus, but the screenshots alone do not identify which provider creates each duplicate.
Image Resizer may have a separate cause because it does not expose the same extended-only setting as File Locksmith and PowerRename.
issue_context.analysis: File Locksmith and PowerRename each declare a windows.fileExplorerContextMenus package verb and also have classic shell handlers. Their modern IExplorerCommand implementations hide themselves when extended-only is selected, while their classic IContextMenu implementations gate on CMF_EXTENDEDVERBS. Image Resizer likewise declares a package-backed file-explorer verb and runtime-registers a classic extension. This confirms multiple providers that warrant a surface-by-surface test, but it does not prove which provider is shown twice or why the extended-only commands disappear. The existing #20255 and #49416 reports cover partial symptoms; neither establishes a released all-tools fix.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body, all five comments, attached menu screenshots, labels, and latest activity; the issue is open and unassigned.

Inspected FileLocksmithContextMenu/AppxManifest.xml and FileLocksmithContextMenu/dllmain.cpp, plus FileLocksmithExt/ExplorerCommand.cpp and PowerToysModule.cpp, for modern and classic visibility guards.
Inspected PowerRenameContextMenu/AppxManifest.xml and PowerRenameContextMenu/dllmain.cpp, plus PowerRenameExt.cpp, for its package-backed and classic registration paths.

Inspected ImageResizerContextMenu/AppxManifest.xml, imageresizer/dllmain.cpp, and ContextMenuHandler.cpp; Image Resizer registers both the package and classic extension, and the handler has no matching extended-only setting.
Reviewed related #20255 and #49416 as partial scope only; no verified fix covers all reported tools and menu modes.

information_gaps.information: Which modern or classic provider creates each duplicate or missing command, and whether the same behavior recurs after a supported update
information_gaps.why_needed: The three utilities have different registration and visibility paths, so the fix should target only the provider proven to be incorrect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Run the supplied menu-mode matrix on a disposable Store-install account and compare package/classic-handler registrations before and after update, without removing production-user registry entries.

judgment.rationale: The report already supplies a concrete menu-mode comparison and screenshots, and the new comment adds a hypothesis rather than evidence of a complete existing fix. Reproduce each tool and shell surface separately before finalizing a code-level design.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the three-tool modern/classic menu matrix and correlate every entry with its registered provider; do not close this as a blanket duplicate or use registry-removal workarounds.
evidence: The issue includes screenshots showing the combined and extended-only menu behavior on PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Store.
Current source contains package-backed and classic shell paths for all three utilities, with different mode guards.
The latest community theory does not establish a provider-level cause; related issues cover only portions of the reported scope.

reproduce.title: Check three utilities on modern and classic Explorer menus
reproduce.module: File Locksmith, PowerRename, and Image Resizer
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare the reported PowerToys 0.100.2 Microsoft Store build with current stable on Windows 11.
prerequisites: Use a disposable Windows user account with the Store installation and the affected utilities enabled.
Create a harmless local image file and a folder.
setup: Preserve the user's existing settings and registrations; do not run registry-removal workarounds.
steps: With File Locksmith and PowerRename set to appear in both default and extended menus, open the default menu and Show more options for the image file and folder; count each command separately.
Set File Locksmith and PowerRename to extended-only and repeat both menu surfaces for the image file and folder.
Record Image Resizer separately because it does not expose the same extended-only setting.
Correlate each visible item with its package-backed or classic handler, then repeat after a supported Store update or repair in the disposable account.
reproduce.expected_result: Each enabled command appears exactly once on its configured supported menu surface. Any missing or duplicated item is linked to a specific provider, and an update does not recreate a removed entry.
